```text
hc - run programs and coding agents in terminals that stay alive

Usage: hc <command> [options]
       hc               pick a terminal and attach (new… on top)

Terminals
  run <cmd|template> [task]   run it and wait like a shell (--bg: don't wait)
  ls                          list live terminals (--all: finished too)
  get <t>                     show one terminal
  attach [t]                  put this terminal on it (ctrl+\ detaches)
  read <t>                    print its screen and history
  kill <t>                    end its program
  rm <t>                      remove a finished terminal
  label <t> k=v...            set labels
  keep <t> [--off]            replace lost programs with a shell (also run --keep)
                              signal death recovers too; streams end on loss, reattach

Talk to programs
  send <t> <text>             paste text and press enter
  keys <t> <keys...>          press keys: enter, esc, up, ctrl+c
  interrupt <t>               press the stop key, report what happened
  wait <t>                    wait until it stops working (--output X: until it prints X,
                              --children: your helpers). Use it instead of sleep.
  put <t> <file>              send a file beside it, print where it landed

No terminal
  exec [--on m] <cmd>         run it, print exactly what it wrote, exit with its code
                              (-i: feed it what is piped in)
  file read|write|edit [--on m] <path>
                              a file here or there: print it, write what is piped
                              in, or replace exact text (--old X --new Y)

More
  templates                   list templates
  events                      follow changes live
  server start|stop|status|restart
                              stop parks kept terminals; next core start gives them shells
  update [--version X|--from <file>]   latest release, at least X, or a build
  machine add|ls|login|update|rename|rm   other machines, over ssh or a command
                              (--via 'fly ssh console -a x --pty=false -C')
  connect                     the API over stdin/stdout (ssh box hc connect)
  schema                      the API as JSON Schema, for app builders

<t> is an address like t7 or t1b, or a name. In a terminal, attach, read, get,
kill, rm, wait and interrupt pick one when it's left out.
Options: --json (default when piped; run and read print text), -V --version,
--licenses (what hc includes, and their licenses).
Per command: hc <command> --help
Settings: ~/.config/herdr-core/config.toml. notes = false: hc types nothing
on its own (no notes to parent agents, no <hc> tags on messages).
shell = ["nu"] overrides the shell for new terminals and keep recovery.

Examples
  hc run --on vps "cd app && npm test"     like ssh, in a terminal that stays
  hc run --bg claude                       Claude Code in a new terminal
  hc attach t3                             take it over
  hc run reviewer "review src/x.rs"        a template with a task
```

```text
	if row, ok := m.currentTask(); ok {

			return func() tea.Msg { return actionMsg{err: err} }
		}
		t := row.Task

			opened, err := m.actions.Open(context.Background(), t)
			return actionMsg{status: opened.Status, cd: opened.Directory, activate: opened.RuntimeHandle, err: err}
		}
	}
	if r, ok := m.currentRepo(); ok {
		return func() tea.Msg {
			opened, err := m.actions.OpenRepo(context.Background(), r)
			return actionMsg{status: opened.Status, cd: opened.Directory, activate: opened.RuntimeHandle, err: err}
		}
	}
	if item, ok := m.currentRepoItem(); ok && item.child() {
		checkout, _ := item.checkout()
		dir := checkout.Worktree.Path
		return func() tea.Msg {
			if !checkout.Exists || checkout.Worktree.Prunable {
				return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("worktree checkout is missing or prunable: %s", dir)}
			}
			if m.actions.OpenCheckout == nil {
				return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("opening linked worktrees is unavailable")}
			}
			opened, err := m.actions.OpenCheckout(context.Background(), item.Repo, checkout)
			return actionMsg{status: opened.Status, cd: opened.Directory, activate: opened.RuntimeHandle, err: err}

	if r, ok := m.currentTry(); ok {

			return func() tea.Msg {
				return tryActionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("Try %s is %s on this host", r.Item.DisplayName(), r.Where())}
			}
		}
		return m.applyTry(TryRequest{Action: TryOpen, ID: r.reference()})
	}
	if r, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok {

			return nil // c is the explicit clone action

			opened, err := m.actions.OpenRemote(context.Background(), r)
			return actionMsg{status: opened.Status, cd: opened.Directory, activate: opened.RuntimeHandle, err: err}

// Activate focuses a workspace and then mirrors hhere's client behavior:
// inside Herdr the existing client switches immediately; outside Herdr a new
// client attaches after the caller has left any alternate-screen UI.
func (h *Herdr) Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
	if handle == "" {
		return nil
	}
	if err := h.Focus(ctx, handle); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if os.Getenv("HERDR_ENV") != "" {
		return nil
	}
	return runInteractive(ctx, h.bin)
}

// Focus selects a workspace on the ordinary local adapter. Session-scoped
// remote preparation forbids this server-wide operation; its caller must use
// an explicit native client activation capability separately.
func (h *Herdr) Focus(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
	if h.session != "" {
		return errors.New("scoped remote preparation cannot change server-wide client focus")
	}
	if handle == "" {
		return nil
	}
	return h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "focus", handle)
}
```

```text
// ErrUnavailable reports a backend that is not usable on this machine.
type ErrUnavailable struct{ Backend, Reason string }

func (e *ErrUnavailable) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("runtime %s unavailable: %s", e.Backend, e.Reason)
}

// Select resolves a configured backend name to a Runtime.
//
// "auto" prefers the richest backend that is actually available: herdr (which
// models workspaces, worktrees and agent sessions), then tmux, then zellij,
// then None.
// None is always available so dev never hard-fails for lack of a multiplexer.
func Select(backend string) Runtime {
	herdr, tmux, zellij, none := NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), NewZellij(), None{}
	switch backend {
	case "herdr":
		return herdr
	case "tmux":
		return tmux
	case "zellij":
		return zellij
	case "none":
		return none
	case "", "auto":
		if herdr.Available() {
			return herdr
		}
		if tmux.Available() {
			return tmux
		}
		if zellij.Available() {
			return zellij
		}
		return none
	}
	return none
}

// All returns every backend, for `dev doctor` to report on.
func All() []Runtime { return []Runtime{NewHerdr(), NewTmux(), NewZellij(), None{}} }

// haveBinary reports whether name is on PATH.
func haveBinary(name string) bool {
	_, err := exec.LookPath(name)
	return err == nil
}

// runInteractive connects a multiplexer client directly to dev's terminal.
// Runtime protocol calls use captured stdout/stderr; attach clients must not,
// because they own the terminal until the user detaches.
func runInteractive(ctx context.Context, bin string, args ...string) error {
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...)
	cmd.Stdin, cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = os.Stdin, os.Stdout, os.Stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %w", bin, strings.Join(args, " "), err)
	}
	return nil
}
```

```text
func newRepoOpenCmd(app *App) *cobra.Command {
	cmd := &cobra.Command{
		Use:   "open <repo>",
		Short: "Open a repository in the runtime",
		Args:  cobra.ExactArgs(1),
		RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
			ctx := ctxOf()
			r, _, err := resolveRepoRef(app, args[0])
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			rt := app.Runtime()
			opened, err := openCheckout(ctx, rt, r.Path, r.Name)
			if err != nil {
				return err
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "%s  %s", r.Name, config.Contract(r.Path))
			if rt.Name() != "none" {
				fmt.Fprintf(app.Out, "  (%s %s)", rt.Name(), opened.Handle)
			}
			fmt.Fprintln(app.Out)
			if rt.Name() == "none" {
				return app.cdDirective(r.Path)
			}
			return activateRuntime(ctx, rt, opened.Handle)
		},
	}
	cmd.ValidArgsFunction = completeRepos(app)
	return cmd
```

```text
func (m Model) executeDashboardAction(action listAction) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
```

````text
Herdr
== /Applications/Herdr.app/Contents/MacOS/Herdr
herdr-app: the Herdr desktop app. With no arguments it opens the window.

Usage:
  herdr-app                        open the window
  herdr-app ls                     spaces, their tabs and terminals, in the open window
  herdr-app do <command> [args]    run a command: --name api --argv '["pi"]', or one JSON object
  herdr-app feedback <text>        draft feedback for the person to review and send
  herdr-app commands               every command, its arguments, what it does
  herdr-app status                 what the window shows, and any errors
  herdr-app shot [file.png]        save the current window frame (default: herdr-shot.png)
  herdr-app check <mod folder>     load a mod once and report what's wrong
  herdr-app --skill                Agent Skill: driving the window, and where hc fits
  herdr-app --version

The terminals run in herdr-core (`hc`), which keeps them alive when the
window closes. `hc --help`: start, read, wait on and talk to terminals and
agents. The app shows them and arranges them in spaces and tabs.

Home: ~/.config/herdr-app (HERDR_APP_HOME picks another).
# hc manual (herdr-core)

The current manual for herdr-core's CLI, `hc`. It is not `herdr`, the older
terminal multiplexer.

# hc: programs and agents that stay alive

`hc` runs programs in persistent terminals. People can attach and take over.
It does not arrange windows; use `herdr-app --skill` for that.
`$HC_TERMINAL_ID` is your address. Terminals you start are your children.
They end when you end, unless started with `--outlive-parent`.
`<t>` below means an ID (`t7`), a name (`review`), or `machine/t7`.
Piped output is JSON except `run`, `exec`, `read`, and `file read` (text).
Use `hc <command> --help` for exact arguments; `hc --help` lists commands.

## Delegate a task

First check `hc templates`: ready-made roles may include `reviewer`,
`simplifier`, or implementers. Use one that fits. Templates are Markdown
files in `~/.config/herdr-core/templates/<name>.md`: frontmatter has `name`,
`description`, `command` (including model); the body supplies instructions.

```sh
hc run --bg --name review --cwd /path/to/repo reviewer "Review only src/x.rs. Read-only; no subagents. Report findings with hc send $HC_TERMINAL_ID when done or stuck."
```

- Always use `--bg` for agents: without it, their whole screen streams into
  your output. Give each agent a name and an exact scope.
- Run agents interactively, never `pi -p` or another one-shot print mode.
  They must remain watchable, steerable, and available for another turn.
- Do not let children start more agents unless you explicitly assign that.
- Put the first task in `run`: a send to a booting agent can be dropped.
  Templates combine their instructions and your task into the first message.
- Without a fitting template, start an interactive agent directly:

```sh
hc run --bg --name fix --cwd /path/to/repo claude "Fix the failing test in x.rs; do not edit other files or start agents. Report with hc send $HC_TERMINAL_ID when done or stuck."
```

A plain launch also works, but wait for readiness before sending its task:

```sh
hc run --bg --name helper pi --provider openai-codex --model gpt-6.1-sol --thinking medium
hc wait helper
hc send helper "Inspect x.rs only. No subagents. Report with hc send $HC_TERMINAL_ID when done or stuck."
```

Check `first_message.sent` in a launch with a task. If false, the task was
NOT sent: `hc read <t>`; resolve readiness first (a trust dialog may need
`hc keys <t> down enter`), then send the task. Do not blindly resend after a
failed send: it may still have arrived; read first.

## Talk, wait, and collect results

```sh
hc ls                              # all live terminals, not just yours
hc get review                      # one terminal's observed state/status
hc send review "Focus on the first bug"
hc send --wait review "Recheck the fix"
hc read --lines 100 review          # screen plus history; waits return status only
hc interrupt review                # stop its current turn, not the process
```

`read --lines 0` reads only the visible screen. History reads may scroll a
full-screen app, then restore its view. While its status is `working`,
`blocked` or `error`, history reads return only the screen immediately,
marked incomplete with `why` set to that status; no scroll input is sent.

Keep doing useful work while children work. When you need their results:

```sh
hc wait --children all             # until none is working, or a message interrupts
hc wait --children any             # next child's news or a message to you
```

Never sleep or poll to wait for anything hc runs: `hc wait <t>` (it stops
working or exits), `hc wait <t> --output X` (it prints X, e.g. a server is
ready), `hc wait --children` (your helpers). Wait can return before all
children finish:
- `reason: message`: the message arrives as your next input, possibly late;
````

````text
# herdr-app: drive the person's window

Herdr shows spaces, tabs and panes. herdr-core (`hc`) runs their terminals
and keeps them alive when the window closes. Use `herdr-app` only to change
what the person sees. For starting, reading, messaging, waiting on or cleaning
up agents and programs, read `hc --skill` and use hc.
Your terminal address is `$HC_TERMINAL_ID`; it is not a pane ID.

## Inspect before acting

```sh
herdr-app ls          # spaces > tabs > terminals, including pane IDs
herdr-app status      # current layout, focus, overlays, zoom and file/mod errors
herdr-app commands    # available commands, arguments and descriptions
```

`ls` and `status` talk to the running window, not a new app. `commands`
prints the built-in command list even without an open window. Do not launch bare
`herdr-app` to inspect it: that opens or raises the window. Do not stop,
signal or restart the person's app or core. A window closing does not kill
its terminals.

`app.check_updates` checks for newer releases. Settings reports "Up to date"
only after a successful check; on failure, check the connection and retry.
Package-managed cores are checked but updated through their package manager.
Dismiss a core update error with its × or `overlay.close {id:"core-update-error"}`;
it stays dismissed until the error changes or the update recovers.

## Show something when asked

New spaces and tabs are shown immediately: only create them when asked.
To start one the person will look at later without moving them there, pass
`--focus false`:

```sh
herdr-app do space.new --name eng-123 --folder ~/code/app/eng-123 --argv '["claude"]' --task "Implement ENG-123" --focus false
```

Pick an explicit, useful name for every new space and tab; don't rely on
default names. Use IDs from `ls` rather than guessing or acting on the wrong
focused pane.

```sh
herdr-app do space.new --name api --folder /path/to/api
herdr-app do tab.new --name "fix login" --argv '["claude"]' --task "Look at the login bug"
herdr-app do pane.split --direction right --pane p12
herdr-app do agent.focus --terminal t7
herdr-app do agent.select --index 3
```

`agent.select` uses the same navigation order as `agent.next` (1 = first).
In `keys.json`, `agent.select:3` selects the third agent in that order.

For a remote space:

```sh
herdr-app do space.new --name "remote api" --machine vps --folder /srv/api
```

The folder is on that machine; tabs and splits in the space stay there.
New-space keys and clicks follow the focused space's machine. Script commands
without `--machine` still use this computer; `--machine ''` explicitly chooses it.
The agent menu checks and starts agents in the remote Unix user's
login/interactive shell (sh, bash, zsh, dash, ksh or fish), including its
configured PATH. Other shells keep the sh launcher.
`terminal.open --folder /path --place down` starts the split in that folder,
including when `--argv` supplies a program. Without `--folder`, it follows the
focused terminal's folder. If an inherited local folder was deleted, new spaces,
tabs and splits retry in that machine's home. An explicit invalid folder
still fails.
`hc machine ls` lists machines. Use `hc run --on vps ...`, `hc exec --on vps ...`
and `hc file ... --on vps ...` for remote work, not your local file tools.

`do` accepts `--key value` arguments (JSON for arrays/objects) or one JSON
object. Unknown argument names fail and list valid names. Target IDs (`id`,
`pane`, `space`, `target`, `terminal`) must be strings; other non-null types fail before
the current-target default can apply. Null keeps its omitted-argument meaning.
Use `commands` to confirm the command's exact shape:

```sh

herdr-app 0.1.18
````

```text
// Package runtime abstracts the terminal multiplexer that hosts a checkout.
//
// dev deliberately owns no terminal state of its own. A runtime is where a
// task is *live*; the durable facts live in git and in the task registry. That
// separation is the whole point: closing a runtime session must never feel
// like abandoning a task, so every adapter here is expected to be lossy and
// re-derivable.
package runtime
import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
)
// Pane is one terminal surface inside a runtime session.
type Pane struct {
	ID           string
	TabID        string
	TerminalID   string
	CWD          string
	ShellCWD     string
	Agent        string
	AgentName    string
	AgentStatus  string
	AgentSession string
	Process      *PaneProcessObservation
}
// Session is one live workspace/session of a runtime backend.
type Session struct {
	// Handle is the backend's own identifier (a herdr workspace id, a tmux
	// session name). Opaque to the rest of dev.
	Handle string
	Label  string
	// Herdr's first-class workspace identity is independent of pane cwd.
	// An observed parent/generic workspace must not be retired as a child.
	WorkspaceIdentityObserved bool
	WorkspaceCheckout         string
	WorkspaceLinked           bool
	// Dirs lists the working directories observed in this session. A session
	// can span several (multiple panes), which is why this is not a single
	// value.
	Dirs []string
	// AgentStatus is the backend's view of agent activity, when it has one:
	// "working", "idle", "done", "waiting". Empty when unsupported.
	AgentStatus string
	// AgentSessions lists resumable agent context ids, e.g. "claude:<uuid>".
	AgentSessions []string
	// Panes retain the exact runtime IDs and cwd values used for caller and
	// mixed-workspace retirement checks.
	Panes   []Pane
	Focused bool
}
// Covers reports whether the session has a pane rooted at or under dir.
func (s Session) Covers(dir string) bool {
	for _, d := range s.Dirs {
		// A pane inside the repository makes it live. The inverse is not
		// true: a generic pane at $HOME does not make every repository below
		// $HOME active.
		if inside, err := pathx.Contains(dir, d); err == nil && inside {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}
// OpenResult is the transient result of making a checkout live. Handle may be
// persisted by callers, but the pane belongs to this one creation response and
// must never be treated as durable state.
type OpenResult struct {
	Handle     string
	Surface    string
	Opened     bool
	Created    bool
	RootPaneID string
}
// AgentActivity is one recognized live coding agent occupying a runtime pane.
// Every activity returned by a backend is occupied regardless of Status; idle,
// done and unknown describe lifecycle state, not permission to share a checkout.
type AgentActivity struct {
	PaneID      string
	WorkspaceID string
	Agent       string
	Name        string
	Status      string
	CWD         string
	// Session is the runtime-reported agent session identity as
	// "provider:id", empty unless the backend reports an exact session id.
	Session string
}
// AgentActivityLister is an optional runtime capability. Core runtimes need not
// know about agents; Herdr implements it because its pane model can identify the
// exact process and checkout involved.
type AgentActivityLister interface {
	AgentActivities(ctx context.Context) ([]AgentActivity, error)
}
// CurrentPaneResolver is an optional runtime capability for resolving the live
// pane behind inherited caller context. Herdr pane IDs can change after a move,
// so collision exclusions must not trust HERDR_PANE_ID alone.
type CurrentPaneResolver interface {
	CurrentPaneID(ctx context.Context) (string, error)
}
// Activator is the optional interactive half of opening a runtime surface.
// Open deliberately remains detached so creation commands can run in the
// background. Navigation commands call Activate after their own terminal UI
// has been torn down: inside a multiplexer this switches the current client;
// outside it attaches a new client and blocks until the user detaches.
type Activator interface {
	Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
}
// PaneRunner is the optional exact-pane command surface. The command is shell
// text for the pane's existing interactive shell, not argv for a child process
// started by dev. Implementations must not include command text in errors.
type PaneRunner interface {
	RunInPane(ctx context.Context, paneID, command string) error
}
// PaneCloser is an optional exact-pane cleanup surface. Callers must freshly
// verify pane identity and agent state before using it.
type PaneCloser interface {
	ClosePane(ctx context.Context, paneID string) error
}
// ExternalCoordinatorOpener creates a fresh, caller-external command surface.
// A reused workspace is never acceptable because destructive coordination must
// have an exact root pane from the same creation response.
type ExternalCoordinatorOpener interface {
	OpenExternalCoordinator(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error)
}
// Runtime is the contract every backend satisfies. Adapters must degrade
// gracefully: an unavailable backend returns errors rather than panicking, and
// List on an idle backend returns an empty slice, not an error.
type Runtime interface {
	// Name is the backend identifier used in config and in `dev doctor`.
	Name() string
	// Available reports whether this backend can be used on this machine right
	// now (binary installed and, where relevant, a server reachable).
	Available() bool
	// Open makes dir live. Its result distinguishes a newly created surface from
	// a reused one and may carry a root pane proven by that same create response.
	Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error)
	// Close ends the session without touching the checkout, the branch or the
	// task entry.
	Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error
	// List enumerates live sessions.
	List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error)
	// Annotate attaches display-only metadata to a session (state, next
	// action). Backends without a metadata channel implement this as a no-op.
	Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error
}
// WorktreeOpener is implemented by backends that understand git worktrees and
// can present one as a first-class session grouped under its parent repo.
// dev always creates the worktree itself — this only surfaces it.
type WorktreeOpener interface {
	OpenWorktree(ctx context.Context, path, label string) (OpenResult, error)
```

````markdown
# herdr-core 支援：宿主偵測、Open target picker、Go-to-folder、`herdr-core` runtime backend

## Context 背景

現在的 Herdr 生態有三個不同的產品，但 dev 只認得第一個：

| 產品 | 環境標記 | 控制介面 |
|---|---|---|
| herdr（classic TUI multiplexer，v0.9.5） | `HERDR_ENV=1`、`HERDR_PANE_ID`… | `herdr workspace …`（現有 `internal/runtime/herdr.go`） |
| herdr-core（`hc`，v0.1.17）+ 官方 **Herdr Desktop**（`herdr-app`，v0.1.18） | `HC_TERMINAL_ID`、`HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET`、`HC_SCOPE`；terminal labels 有 `herdr.space` / `herdr.tab` | `hc ls/get/run/label --json`、`herdr-app ls`、`herdr-app do space.new/space.select/…` |
| **Sheprd**（第三方 GUI，跟 Herdr Desktop 是不同產品） | 自己的 control socket `~/.local/state/herdr/gpui/control.sock` | `sheprd open DIR`、`sheprd status --json` |

問題：
1. 在 herdr-core terminal 裡（沒有 `HERDR_ENV`），TUI 按 Enter 時，`runtime.Select("auto")` 會選到 herdr，先建立 herdr workspace，然後 `Herdr.Activate`（`internal/runtime/herdr.go:370`）因為 `HERDR_ENV` 是空的，會**在 GUI pane 裡 attach 一個 herdr TUI client**。此外 Enter 只會開到一個目標。
2. TUI 沒有獨立的「cd 到資料夾」action。只有 runtime 為 `none` 時，Enter 才會透過 `m.chosen` → `app.cdDirective` 進行 cd。
3. 完全沒有 hc 整合：不會用到 hc 的 terminal/agent 觀察，也不會用到 Herdr Desktop 的 space。

目標：正確偵測宿主；Enter 改成 picker，可選 runtime、Herdr Desktop、herdr TUI、Sheprd 或 cd；新增 Go-to-folder 快捷鍵；新增完整的 `herdr-core` runtime backend。

## Phase 1 — 宿主偵測 Host context detection

新檔 `internal/runtime/host.go`：

```go
type HostKind string // "herdr", "herdr-core", "tmux", "zellij", "plain"
type HostContext struct {
    Kind       HostKind
    GUI        string // "herdr-desktop", "sheprd", "unknown", ""
    TerminalID string // HC_TERMINAL_ID
    Socket     string // HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET
    Evidence   []string
}
func DetectHost(ctx context.Context) HostContext
```

- 判斷順序：`HERDR_ENV=1` → herdr；`HC_TERMINAL_ID` 有值 → herdr-core；`TMUX` → tmux；`ZELLIJ` → zellij；都沒有 → plain。若同時有多個標記（例如 herdr-core 裡又開 tmux），以最內層為準，並把所有證據記進 `Evidence`。
- 判斷 GUI：只跑一次 bounded `hc get $HC_TERMINAL_ID --json`（timeout 約 1s）。labels 有 `herdr.space` 就是 `herdr-desktop`。若 Sheprd control socket 存在（只做 stat，不執行任何東西），且 `sheprd status --json` 能回報這個 terminal，就是 `sheprd`。其他情況一律是 `unknown`，不猜測（fail closed，unknown 不會變成某個 fact）。
- 呈現：`dev doctor` 的 runtime 區段加一行 `host: herdr-core (Herdr Desktop, t2)`。TUI status/header 也顯示 host。
- 測試：用注入 env 加 fake `hc` binary 的 table test（沿用 `internal/runtime/native_fixture_test.go` 的 fixture 方式）。

## Phase 2 — `herdr-core` runtime backend

新檔 `internal/runtime/herdrcore.go`，實作 `Runtime`、`Activator`、`AgentActivityLister`、`CurrentPaneResolver`。

- `Name()`：`"herdr-core"`。`Available()`：PATH 上有 `herdr-core` 或 `hc` binary（注意使用者的 `hc` 可能是 shell alias，所以優先找 `herdr-core`），而且 `HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET` 存在，或 `hc server status --json` 回報正在執行。
- `List`：`hc ls --json`，terminal 依 label `herdr.space` 分組成 `Session`。`Handle` 是 space id；沒有 space 的 terminal 自成一個 session，`Handle` 用 terminal address。`Dirs` 包含 `cwd` 和 `foreground.cwd`。`Panes[].TerminalID` 用 address，`AgentStatus` 用 `status.state`。
- `Open(dir,label)`：
  - 有 Herdr Desktop 時，用 `herdr-app ls` 找 folder 與 dir 相同（以 `pathx` 正規化比較）的 space 重用，`Created=false`。找不到就跑 `herdr-app do space.new --name <label> --folder <dir> --focus false`，`Created=true`，handle 是 space id。
  - 沒有 GUI 時，跑 `hc run --bg --no-parent --outlive-parent --keep --name dev-<slug> --cwd <dir>` 開一個 shell terminal，handle 是 terminal address。
- `Activate(handle)`：space 用 `herdr-app do space.select --id <id>`。terminal handle 在 HC terminal 內時回報位址、不 attach（避免巢狀）；在外面時用 `runInteractive(hc attach <t>)`（`internal/runtime/runtime.go` 現有 helper）。
- `Close`：只關 dev 開的 space，必須有 `dev.*` label 證明。執行 `herdr-app do space.close --id … --confirmed`，前置 agent 檢查沿用 taskflow 現有的 guard。
- `Annotate`：對 session 內的 terminal 執行 `hc label <t> dev.state=… dev.next=…`。
- `AgentActivities`：讀 `hc ls --json` 的 `agent`/`status`。任何被辨識的 agent 都算占用，跟 Behavioral contracts 一致。
- `CurrentPaneID`：做一次 fresh `hc get $HC_TERMINAL_ID`，確認 terminal 存在後回傳。
- **刻意不實作** `WorktreeOpener`、`ExternalCoordinatorOpener`、`PaneRunner`、`PaneCloser`。parallel launch 繼續 fail closed，文件要寫明。
- `Select`（`internal/runtime/runtime.go:184`）：`case "herdr-core"` 回傳新 backend。`auto` 的新順序是：在 HC terminal 內且 herdr-core 可用時優先選 herdr-core，`HERDR_ENV=1` 時選 herdr，其他情況維持原順序。`All()` 也加入它。
- `internal/config/config.go:511` 的 validation 加上 `herdr-core`。`--runtime` flag 的說明字串要同步，然後跑 `make skill-sync`。
- 測試：參考 `herdr_test.go`，用 fake `hc`/`herdr-app` script 驗證 argv 與 JSON 解析、space 重用與新建、Close 的 label guard、HC 內 Activate 不會 attach。

## Phase 3 — Enter 的 Open target picker

**目標清單**由 CLI 計算，新檔 `internal/cli/open_targets.go`：

| ID | 條件 | 動作 |
|---|---|---|
| `runtime` | 永遠存在 | 現有 `openResolved` 路徑（`internal/cli/tui.go:382`） |
| `herdr-desktop` | `herdr-app` 存在且 herdr-core 可用 | herdr-core backend 的 Open 加 Activate |
| `herdr` | herdr binary 存在 | 強制使用 herdr backend；不在 HERDR_ENV 內時，提示會 attach client |
| `sheprd` | `sheprd` binary 存在 | `sheprd open DIR`；exit code 3/7 轉成可讀的錯誤訊息 |
| `cd` | 永遠存在 | `OpenResult{Directory: dir}` |

與 `runtime` 解析結果相同的目標要合併，不重複列出。

**設定**（`internal/config` 的 `TUI` struct 新增 `Open OpenTable`）：

```toml
[tui.open]
mode = "ask"        # ask | default；ask 只在有 ≥2 個不同目標時才跳 picker
default = "runtime" # picker 的預選項，也是 mode=default 時使用的目標
```

**TUI 改動**：
- `tui.Actions`（`internal/tui/model.go:177-183`）新增 `OpenTargets func(dir string) []OpenTarget`。`Open`、`OpenRepo`、`OpenCheckout`、`OpenRemote` 多一個 `target string` 參數（這是內部 API，可以直接改）。
- `openSelected()`（`internal/tui/model.go:4302`）：先算出目標清單。只有一個目標，或 mode=default 時直接執行；否則開 chooser。chooser 沿用 `listActionCopy`（"copy repository data…"）的選單實作，數字鍵直選，Enter 確認，Esc 取消。
- Sheprd 與 Herdr Desktop 是 GUI 端切換，行為維持一致：完成後走現有 `actionMsg{activate}`，退出 TUI 再 activate。Sheprd 不需要 handle，所以直接在 callback 裡執行，然後 status 回報。
- Fleet row 的 Enter 不變，仍走 `fleetnav`。

## Phase 4 — Go-to-folder action

- `internal/tui/action_definitions.go` 新增 `listActionCd`，標籤是「cd to folder」，按鍵 `C`（已確認沒被占用；小寫 `c` 已用於 edit next 和 clone，`g` 已用於 home）。
- 適用範圍：Tasks（checkout 存在）、Repos（repo 或 worktree child）、Tries（`Present()`）、Remote（`Cloned()`）。
````

````text
## Approved Plan:
# herdr-core 支援：宿主偵測、Open target picker、Go-to-folder、`herdr-core` runtime backend

## Context 背景

現在的 Herdr 生態有三個不同的產品，但 dev 只認得第一個：

| 產品 | 環境標記 | 控制介面 |
|---|---|---|
| herdr（classic TUI multiplexer，v0.9.5） | `HERDR_ENV=1`、`HERDR_PANE_ID`… | `herdr workspace …`（現有 `internal/runtime/herdr.go`） |
| herdr-core（`hc`，v0.1.17）+ 官方 **Herdr Desktop**（`herdr-app`，v0.1.18） | `HC_TERMINAL_ID`、`HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET`、`HC_SCOPE`；terminal labels 有 `herdr.space` / `herdr.tab` | `hc ls/get/run/label --json`、`herdr-app ls`、`herdr-app do space.new/space.select/…` |
| **Sheprd**（第三方 GUI，跟 Herdr Desktop 是不同產品） | 自己的 control socket `~/.local/state/herdr/gpui/control.sock` | `sheprd open DIR`、`sheprd status --json` |

問題：
1. 在 herdr-core terminal 裡（沒有 `HERDR_ENV`），TUI 按 Enter 時，`runtime.Select("auto")` 會選到 herdr，先建立 herdr workspace，然後 `Herdr.Activate`（`internal/runtime/herdr.go:370`）因為 `HERDR_ENV` 是空的，會**在 GUI pane 裡 attach 一個 herdr TUI client**。此外 Enter 只會開到一個目標。
2. TUI 沒有獨立的「cd 到資料夾」action。只有 runtime 為 `none` 時，Enter 才會透過 `m.chosen` → `app.cdDirective` 進行 cd。
3. 完全沒有 hc 整合：不會用到 hc 的 terminal/agent 觀察，也不會用到 Herdr Desktop 的 space。

目標：正確偵測宿主；Enter 改成 picker，可選 runtime、Herdr Desktop、herdr TUI、Sheprd 或 cd；新增 Go-to-folder 快捷鍵；新增完整的 `herdr-core` runtime backend。

## Phase 1 — 宿主偵測 Host context detection

新檔 `internal/runtime/host.go`：

```go
type HostKind string // "herdr", "herdr-core", "tmux", "zellij", "plain"
type HostContext struct {
    Kind       HostKind
    GUI        string // "herdr-desktop", "sheprd", "unknown", ""
    TerminalID string // HC_TERMINAL_ID
    Socket     string // HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET
    Evidence   []string
}
func DetectHost(ctx context.Context) HostContext
```

- 判斷順序：`HERDR_ENV=1` → herdr；`HC_TERMINAL_ID` 有值 → herdr-core；`TMUX` → tmux；`ZELLIJ` → zellij；都沒有 → plain。若同時有多個標記（例如 herdr-core 裡又開 tmux），以最內層為準，並把所有證據記進 `Evidence`。
- 判斷 GUI：只跑一次 bounded `hc get $HC_TERMINAL_ID --json`（timeout 約 1s）。labels 有 `herdr.space` 就是 `herdr-desktop`。若 Sheprd control socket 存在（只做 stat，不執行任何東西），且 `sheprd status --json` 能回報這個 terminal，就是 `sheprd`。其他情況一律是 `unknown`，不猜測（fail closed，unknown 不會變成某個 fact）。
- 呈現：`dev doctor` 的 runtime 區段加一行 `host: herdr-core (Herdr Desktop, t2)`。TUI status/header 也顯示 host。
- 測試：用注入 env 加 fake `hc` binary 的 table test（沿用 `internal/runtime/native_fixture_test.go` 的 fixture 方式）。

## Phase 2 — `herdr-core` runtime backend

新檔 `internal/runtime/herdrcore.go`，實作 `Runtime`、`Activator`、`AgentActivityLister`、`CurrentPaneResolver`。

- `Name()`：`"herdr-core"`。`Available()`：PATH 上有 `herdr-core` 或 `hc` binary（注意使用者的 `hc` 可能是 shell alias，所以優先找 `herdr-core`），而且 `HC_TERMINAL_SOCKET` 存在，或 `hc server status --json` 回報正在執行。
- `List`：`hc ls --json`，terminal 依 label `herdr.space` 分組成 `Session`。`Handle` 是 space id；沒有 space 的 terminal 自成一個 session，`Handle` 用 terminal address。`Dirs` 包含 `cwd` 和 `foreground.cwd`。`Panes[].TerminalID` 用 address，`AgentStatus` 用 `status.state`。
- `Open(dir,label)`：
  - 有 Herdr Desktop 時，用 `herdr-app ls` 找 folder 與 dir 相同（以 `pathx` 正規化比較）的 space 重用，`Created=false`。找不到就跑 `herdr-app do space.new --name <label> --folder <dir> --focus false`，`Created=true`，handle 是 space id。
  - 沒有 GUI 時，跑 `hc run --bg --no-parent --outlive-parent --keep --name dev-<slug> --cwd <dir>` 開一個 shell terminal，handle 是 terminal address。
- `Activate(handle)`：space 用 `herdr-app do space.select --id <id>`。terminal handle 在 HC terminal 內時回報位址、不 attach（避免巢狀）；在外面時用 `runInteractive(hc attach <t>)`（`internal/runtime/runtime.go` 現有 helper）。
- `Close`：只關 dev 開的 space，必須有 `dev.*` label 證明。執行 `herdr-app do space.close --id … --confirmed`，前置 agent 檢查沿用 taskflow 現有的 guard。
- `Annotate`：對 session 內的 terminal 執行 `hc label <t> dev.state=… dev.next=…`。
- `AgentActivities`：讀 `hc ls --json` 的 `agent`/`status`。任何被辨識的 agent 都算占用，跟 Behavioral contracts 一致。
- `CurrentPaneID`：做一次 fresh `hc get $HC_TERMINAL_ID`，確認 terminal 存在後回傳。
- **刻意不實作** `WorktreeOpener`、`ExternalCoordinatorOpener`、`PaneRunner`、`PaneCloser`。parallel launch 繼續 fail closed，文件要寫明。
- `Select`（`internal/runtime/runtime.go:184`）：`case "herdr-core"` 回傳新 backend。`auto` 的新順序是：在 HC terminal 內且 herdr-core 可用時優先選 herdr-core，`HERDR_ENV=1` 時選 herdr，其他情況維持原順序。`All()` 也加入它。
- `internal/config/config.go:511` 的 validation 加上 `herdr-core`。`--runtime` flag 的說明字串要同步，然後跑 `make skill-sync`。
- 測試：參考 `herdr_test.go`，用 fake `hc`/`herdr-app` script 驗證 argv 與 JSON 解析、space 重用與新建、Close 的 label guard、HC 內 Activate 不會 attach。

## Phase 3 — Enter 的 Open target picker

**目標清單**由 CLI 計算，新檔 `internal/cli/open_targets.go`：

| ID | 條件 | 動作 |
|---|---|---|
````

```text
package runtime

import "context"

// None is the no-multiplexer backend. It is always available, which is what
// guarantees dev's core inventory and worktree commands work on a bare machine
// with nothing but git installed.
//
// Open returns the directory itself as the handle: the shell wrapper installed
// by `dev shell-init` turns that into a cd in the calling shell, since a child
// process can never change its parent's working directory.
type None struct{}

// Name implements Runtime.
func (None) Name() string { return "none" }

// Available implements Runtime; the null backend always is.
func (None) Available() bool { return true }

// Open implements Runtime by reporting the directory to change into. None does
// not open a runtime surface, so the result is never launchable.
func (None) Open(_ context.Context, dir, _ string) (OpenResult, error) {
	return OpenResult{Handle: dir}, nil
}

// Close implements Runtime as a no-op: there is no session to end.
func (None) Close(context.Context, string) error { return nil }

// List implements Runtime; without a multiplexer nothing is tracked as live.
func (None) List(context.Context) ([]Session, error) { return nil, nil }

// Annotate implements Runtime as a no-op.
func (None) Annotate(context.Context, string, map[string]string) error { return nil }
```

```text
package runtime

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"
	"time"
)

// Herdr drives the herdr terminal workspace manager over its CLI, which emits
// JSON on stdout for every subcommand dev needs.
//
// Division of responsibility, deliberately: dev creates worktrees with plain
// `git worktree add` at its own configured path and then asks herdr to *open*
// that path. `herdr worktree create` is not used, because it would put the
// path policy in a second place — and that policy has to hold on machines
// where herdr is not installed at all.
type Herdr struct {
	bin string
	// session is set only for an explicitly scoped remote preparation. Default
	// local runtime behavior continues to use native caller context.
	session string
	// metadataSource namespaces the workspace metadata tokens dev reports.
	metadataSource string
	// runCommand and worktreeSource are test seams for Herdr's JSON protocol
	// and Git parent-workspace source resolution.
	runCommand     func(context.Context, ...string) ([]byte, error)
	processProbe   func(context.Context, ...string) ([]byte, int, error)
	worktreeSource func(context.Context, string) string
}

// NewHerdr returns the herdr adapter.
func NewHerdr() *Herdr { return &Herdr{bin: "herdr", metadataSource: "dev"} }

// WithMetadataSource sets the --source id used for workspace metadata tokens.
func (h *Herdr) WithMetadataSource(src string) *Herdr {
	if src != "" {
		h.metadataSource = src
	}
	return h
}

// Name implements Runtime.
func (h *Herdr) Name() string { return "herdr" }

// Available reports whether the binary exists *and* a server is reachable.
// The binary alone is not enough: every dev call goes through the socket API,
// so a stopped server must degrade to the next backend rather than making
// every command fail.
func (h *Herdr) Available() bool {
	if !haveBinary(h.bin) {
		return false
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	_, err := h.run(ctx, "workspace", "list")
	return err == nil
}

func (h *Herdr) run(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
	return h.runDisplayed(ctx, strings.Join(args, " "), args...)
}

// runDisplayed allows callers carrying sensitive argv to provide a redacted
// description for diagnostics. The real argv still goes to Herdr unchanged.
func (h *Herdr) runDisplayed(ctx context.Context, display string, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
	if h.session != "" {
		args = append([]string{"--session", h.session}, args...)
	}
	if h.runCommand != nil {
		return h.runCommand(ctx, args...)
	}
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, h.bin, args...)
	if h.session != "" {
		cmd.Env = scopedHerdrEnvironment(os.Environ())
	}
	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
		if msg == "" {
			msg = err.Error()
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: %s", display, msg)
	}
	return stdout.Bytes(), nil
}

// herdrEnvelope is the common shape of every herdr CLI JSON response.
type herdrEnvelope struct {
	ID     string          `json:"id"`
	Error  *herdrError     `json:"error"`
	Result json.RawMessage `json:"result"`
}

type herdrError struct {
	Code    string `json:"code"`
	Message string `json:"message"`
}

// call runs a herdr subcommand and decodes result into out.
func (h *Herdr) call(ctx context.Context, out any, args ...string) error {
	return h.callDisplayed(ctx, out, strings.Join(args, " "), args...)
}

func (h *Herdr) callDisplayed(ctx context.Context, out any, display string, args ...string) error {
	raw, err := h.runDisplayed(ctx, display, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if out == nil && len(bytes.TrimSpace(raw)) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	var env herdrEnvelope
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &env); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: unexpected output: %w", display, err)
	}
	if env.Error != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("herdr %s: %s (%s)", display, env.Error.Message, env.Error.Code)
	}
	if out == nil {
		return nil
	}
	return json.Unmarshal(env.Result, out)
}

// RunInPane atomically sends shell command text and Enter to one exact pane.
// The command is intentionally redacted from every diagnostic path.
func (h *Herdr) RunInPane(ctx context.Context, paneID, command string) error {
func (h *Herdr) CurrentPaneID(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
	var res struct {
		Pane herdrPane `json:"pane"`
	}
	if err := h.call(ctx, &res, "pane", "current", "--current"); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	if res.Pane.PaneID == "" {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("herdr pane current --current: response has no pane id")
	}
	return res.Pane.PaneID, nil
}

// AgentActivities implements AgentActivityLister using Herdr's recognized-agent
// inventory. Every returned row is occupied; lifecycle state is descriptive and
// is deliberately not used to decide whether another agent may share its cwd.
func (h *Herdr) AgentActivities(ctx context.Context) ([]AgentActivity, error) {
	var res struct {
		Agents *[]herdrPane `json:"agents"`
	}
	if err := h.call(ctx, &res, "agent", "list"); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if res.Agents == nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("herdr agent list: response has no agents array")
	}
	out := make([]AgentActivity, 0, len(*res.Agents))
	for _, p := range *res.Agents {
		cwd := p.ForegroundCWD
		if cwd == "" {
			cwd = p.CWD
		}
		if cwd == "" {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("herdr agent list: recognized agent in pane %s has no cwd", p.PaneID)
		}
		session := ""
		if p.AgentSession != nil && p.AgentSession.Value != "" && (p.AgentSession.Kind == "" || p.AgentSession.Kind == "id") {
			agent := p.AgentSession.Agent
			if agent == "" {
				agent = p.Agent
			}
			session = agent + ":" + p.AgentSession.Value
		}
		out = append(out, AgentActivity{
			PaneID: p.PaneID, WorkspaceID: p.WorkspaceID,
			Agent: p.Agent, Name: p.Name, Status: p.AgentStatus, CWD: cwd, Session: session,
		})
	}
	return out, nil
}

// Open implements Runtime. An already-open directory is reused rather than
// opened twice. It remains detached; explicit navigation calls Activate.
func (h *Herdr) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
	existing, err := h.List(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return OpenResult{}, err
	}
	for _, s := range existing {
		if s.Covers(dir) {
			return OpenResult{Handle: s.Handle, Surface: "workspace", Opened: true}, nil
		}
	}
	return h.createWorkspace(ctx, dir, label)
}

// OpenExternalCoordinator always creates a fresh workspace. Destructive
// cleanup cannot run in a reused or caller-owned surface.
func (h *Herdr) OpenExternalCoordinator(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
	return h.createWorkspace(ctx, dir, label)
}

func (h *Herdr) createWorkspace(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
func (h *Herdr) Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
	if handle == "" {
		return nil
	}
	return h.call(ctx, nil, "workspace", "close", handle)
}

// Annotate implements Runtime by reporting display-only workspace metadata.
//
// Note for users: a token only renders if the sidebar row layout in
// ~/.config/herdr/config.toml names it, e.g. rows = [[..., "$stage"], ["$next"]].
// Setting a token with no matching layout entry succeeds silently and shows
// nothing.
func (h *Herdr) Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error {
	if handle == "" || len(kv) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	args := []string{"workspace", "report-metadata", handle, "--source", h.metadataSource}
	for k, v := range kv {
		if v == "" {
			args = append(args, "--clear-token", k)
			continue
		}
		args = append(args, "--token", k+"="+v)
	}
	return h.call(ctx, nil, args...)
}

func keys(m map[string]bool) []string {
	if len(m) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	out := make([]string, 0, len(m))
	for k := range m {
		out = append(out, k)
	}
	for i := 1; i < len(out); i++ {
		for j := i; j > 0 && out[j] < out[j-1]; j-- {
			out[j], out[j-1] = out[j-1], out[j]
		}
	}
	return out
}

type herdrCall struct {
	args []string
	out  string
	err  error
}

func scriptedHerdr(t *testing.T, calls ...herdrCall) *Herdr {
	t.Helper()
	index := 0
	h := NewHerdr()
	h.runCommand = func(_ context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
		t.Helper()
		if index >= len(calls) {
			t.Fatalf("unexpected herdr call: %v", args)
		}
		call := calls[index]
		index++
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(args, call.args) {
			t.Fatalf("herdr call %d = %v, want %v", index, args, call.args)
		}
		return []byte(call.out), call.err
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		if index != len(calls) {
			t.Errorf("used %d herdr calls, want %d", index, len(calls))
		}
	})
	return h
}

func TestHerdrListRetainsPaneIdentityAndForegroundCWD(t *testing.T) {
	h := scriptedHerdr(t,
		herdrCall{args: []string{"workspace", "list"}, out: `{"id":"1","result":{"workspaces":[{"workspace_id":"w1","label":"dev","agent_status":"idle"}]}}`},
		herdrCall{args: []string{"pane", "list"}, out: `{"id":"2","result":{"panes":[` +
			`{"pane_id":"w1:p1","workspace_id":"w1","cwd":"/old","foreground_cwd":"/repo","agent":"claude","agent_status":"idle","agent_session":{"agent":"claude","value":"abc"}},` +
			`{"pane_id":"w1:p2","workspace_id":"w1","cwd":"/repo/sub"}` +
			`]}}`},
	)
	sessions, err := h.List(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(sessions) != 1 || len(sessions[0].Panes) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("sessions = %+v", sessions)
	}
```

```go
package runtime

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	goruntime "runtime"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/daviddwlee84/dev-cli/internal/pathx"
)

// HerdrCore drives herdr-core (`hc`), the persistent terminal server behind
// the official Herdr Desktop app, and optionally Herdr Desktop itself
// (`herdr-app`) for the spaces a person sees.
//
// It is a different product from the classic `herdr` multiplexer: terminals
// are addressed as `t7`, the caller's address is HC_TERMINAL_ID, and spaces
// and tabs belong to the desktop window rather than to the server. dev keeps
// the same division of responsibility as with every runtime: it never creates
// or manages Git worktrees here, it only surfaces a checkout path the calling
// flow already selected.
//
// Remote machine terminals (`machine/t7`) are deliberately ignored. Their
// paths live on another host, so they can neither cover nor occupy a local
// checkout.
type HerdrCore struct {
	hcBin  string
	appBin string
	// Test seams for the hc and herdr-app JSON protocols and the inherited
	// caller environment.
	runHC  func(context.Context, ...string) ([]byte, error)
	runApp func(context.Context, ...string) ([]byte, error)
	getenv func(string) string
	// interactive attaches a client to the caller's terminal.
	interactive func(context.Context, string, ...string) error
}

// Labels dev writes on terminals it opened. Close refuses surfaces that lack
// this proof, so a person's own spaces and terminals are never ended by dev.
const (
	herdrCoreOwnedLabel = "dev.owned"
	herdrCoreLabelSpace = "dev."
	herdrCoreMaxGets    = 64
)

// NewHerdrCore returns the herdr-core adapter. The server CLI installs as
// `herdr-core`; `hc` is its documented short name but is often a shell alias,
// so the real binary name is preferred.
func NewHerdrCore() *HerdrCore {
	hc := "herdr-core"
	if !haveBinary(hc) && haveBinary("hc") {
		hc = "hc"
	}
	return &HerdrCore{hcBin: hc, appBin: herdrAppBinary(), getenv: os.Getenv, interactive: runInteractive}
}

// herdrAppBinary locates the Herdr Desktop control CLI: the `herdr-app` link
// the app installs, or the bundled macOS executable.
func herdrAppBinary() string {
	if haveBinary("herdr-app") {
		return "herdr-app"
	}
	if goruntime.GOOS == "darwin" {
		bundled := "/Applications/Herdr.app/Contents/MacOS/Herdr"
		if info, err := os.Stat(bundled); err == nil && !info.IsDir() {
			return bundled
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// Name implements Runtime.
func (h *HerdrCore) Name() string { return "herdr-core" }

// Available reports whether the hc binary exists and its server answers.
// A stopped server must degrade to the next backend instead of failing every
// command, and `server status` never starts one.
func (h *HerdrCore) Available() bool {
	if h.runHC == nil && !haveBinary(h.hcBin) {
		return false
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	_, err := h.hc(ctx, "server", "status", "--json")
	return err == nil
}

// DesktopAvailable reports whether a Herdr Desktop window is running and
// answers. Spaces exist only in that window; without it dev opens plain hc
// terminals instead.
func (h *HerdrCore) DesktopAvailable(ctx context.Context) bool {
	if h.runApp == nil && h.appBin == "" {
		return false
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	_, err := h.app(ctx, "status")
	return err == nil
}

func (h *HerdrCore) hc(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
	if h.runHC != nil {
		return h.runHC(ctx, args...)
	}
	return runJSONCommand(ctx, "hc", h.hcBin, args...)
}

func (h *HerdrCore) app(ctx context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
	if h.runApp != nil {
		return h.runApp(ctx, args...)
	}
	if h.appBin == "" {
		return nil, errors.New("herdr-app: Herdr Desktop is not installed")
	}
	return runJSONCommand(ctx, "herdr-app", h.appBin, args...)
}

func runJSONCommand(ctx context.Context, display, bin string, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...)
	var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
	cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &stdout, &stderr
	if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
		msg := strings.TrimSpace(stderr.String())
		if msg == "" {
			msg = strings.TrimSpace(stdout.String())
		}
		if msg == "" {
			msg = err.Error()
		}
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s %s: %s", display, strings.Join(args, " "), msg)
	}
	return stdout.Bytes(), nil
}

// hcTerminal is one row of `hc ls --json` or the document of `hc get --json`.
// `ls` reports status as a string; `get` reports an object with the
// recognized app and its state.
type hcTerminal struct {
	Address    string            `json:"address"`
	Agent      string            `json:"agent"`
	CWD        string            `json:"cwd"`
	Name       string            `json:"name"`
	State      string            `json:"state"`
	Where      string            `json:"where"`
	Labels     map[string]string `json:"labels"`
	Status     json.RawMessage   `json:"status"`
	Foreground *struct {
		CWD  string `json:"cwd"`
		Name string `json:"name"`
	} `json:"foreground"`
}

func (t hcTerminal) local() bool { return t.Address != "" && !strings.Contains(t.Address, "/") }

// status returns the recognized agent app and its state. A terminal running
// a plain shell has neither.
func (t hcTerminal) status() (app, state string) {
	raw := bytes.TrimSpace(t.Status)
	if len(raw) == 0 || string(raw) == "null" {
		return "", ""
	}
	var s string
	if json.Unmarshal(raw, &s) == nil {
		return t.Agent, s
	}
	var obj struct {
		App   string `json:"app"`
		State string `json:"state"`
	}
	if json.Unmarshal(raw, &obj) == nil {
		if obj.App == "" {
			obj.App = t.Agent
		}
		return obj.App, obj.State
	}
	return "", ""
}

func (t hcTerminal) dirs() []string {
	var out []string
	if t.Foreground != nil && t.Foreground.CWD != "" {
		out = append(out, t.Foreground.CWD)
	}
	if t.CWD != "" && (len(out) == 0 || out[0] != t.CWD) {
		out = append(out, t.CWD)
	}
	return out
}

type hcList struct {
	Terminals *[]hcTerminal `json:"terminals"`
}

// appSpace is one space of `herdr-app ls`.
type appSpace struct {
	ID      string  `json:"id"`
	Name    string  `json:"name"`
	Folder  string  `json:"folder"`
	Machine *string `json:"machine"`
	Active  bool    `json:"active"`
	Tabs    []struct {
		ID        string `json:"id"`
		Name      string `json:"name"`
		Active    bool   `json:"active"`
		Terminals []struct {
			Terminal string  `json:"terminal"`
			Pane     string  `json:"pane"`
			Status   *string `json:"status"`
			App      *string `json:"app"`
		} `json:"terminals"`
	} `json:"tabs"`
}

func (s appSpace) local() bool { return s.Machine == nil || *s.Machine == "" }

func (s appSpace) terminals() []string {
	var out []string
	for _, tab := range s.Tabs {
		for _, t := range tab.Terminals {
			out = append(out, t.Terminal)
		}
	}
	return out
}

type appLayout struct {
	Spaces *[]appSpace `json:"spaces"`
}

// terminals returns the live local terminals with their foreground cwd.
// `hc ls` reports only the shell's cwd, which is not where an agent started
// from that shell is working, so each local terminal is read with `hc get`.
func (h *HerdrCore) terminals(ctx context.Context) ([]hcTerminal, error) {
	raw, err := h.hc(ctx, "ls", "--json")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var list hcList
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &list); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("hc ls: unexpected output: %w", err)
	}
	if list.Terminals == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("hc ls: response has no terminals array")
	}
	var out []hcTerminal
	for _, t := range *list.Terminals {
		if !t.local() || (t.State != "" && t.State != "live") {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, t)
	}
	if len(out) > herdrCoreMaxGets {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("hc ls: %d local terminals exceed the %d dev observes", len(out), herdrCoreMaxGets)
	}
	for i := range out {
		detail, err := h.terminal(ctx, out[i].Address)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out[i] = detail
	}
	return out, nil
}

func (h *HerdrCore) terminal(ctx context.Context, address string) (hcTerminal, error) {
	raw, err := h.hc(ctx, "get", address, "--json")
	if err != nil {
		return hcTerminal{}, err
	}
	var t hcTerminal
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &t); err != nil {
		return hcTerminal{}, fmt.Errorf("hc get %s: unexpected output: %w", address, err)
	}
	if t.Address == "" {
		return hcTerminal{}, fmt.Errorf("hc get %s: response has no address", address)
	}
	return t, nil
}

// spaces returns Herdr Desktop's local spaces, or nil when no window runs.
func (h *HerdrCore) spaces(ctx context.Context) ([]appSpace, error) {
	if !h.DesktopAvailable(ctx) {
		return nil, nil
	}
	raw, err := h.app(ctx, "ls")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var layout appLayout
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &layout); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("herdr-app ls: unexpected output: %w", err)
	}
	if layout.Spaces == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("herdr-app ls: response has no spaces array")
	}
	var out []appSpace
	for _, s := range *layout.Spaces {
		if s.local() && s.ID != "" {
			out = append(out, s)
		}
	}
	return out, nil
}

// List implements Runtime. With Herdr Desktop running, a session is a space
// and its panes are the space's terminals. Terminals no space shows (or every
// terminal when no window runs) are sessions of their own.
func (h *HerdrCore) List(ctx context.Context) ([]Session, error) {
	terminals, err := h.terminals(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	spaces, err := h.spaces(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	byAddress := make(map[string]hcTerminal, len(terminals))
	for _, t := range terminals {
		byAddress[t.Address] = t
	}
	claimed := map[string]bool{}
	var out []Session
	for _, s := range spaces {
		session := Session{Handle: s.ID, Label: s.Name, Focused: s.Active}
		for _, tab := range s.Tabs {
			for _, ref := range tab.Terminals {
				t, ok := byAddress[ref.Terminal]
				if !ok {
					continue
				}
				claimed[t.Address] = true
				session.Panes = append(session.Panes, h.pane(t, tab.ID))
				session.Dirs = appendUnique(session.Dirs, t.dirs()...)
				if _, state := t.status(); state != "" && session.AgentStatus == "" {
					session.AgentStatus = state
				}
			}
		}
		if s.Folder != "" {
			session.Dirs = appendUnique(session.Dirs, s.Folder)
		}
		out = append(out, session)
	}
	for _, t := range terminals {
		if claimed[t.Address] {
			continue
		}
		label := t.Name
		if label == "" {
			label = t.Where
		}
		if label == "" {
			label = t.Address
		}
		_, state := t.status()
		out = append(out, Session{
			Handle: t.Address, Label: label, Dirs: t.dirs(), AgentStatus: state,
			Panes: []Pane{h.pane(t, "")},
		})
	}
	return out, nil
}

func (h *HerdrCore) pane(t hcTerminal, tab string) Pane {
	app, state := t.status()
	p := Pane{ID: t.Address, TabID: tab, TerminalID: t.Address, CWD: t.CWD, ShellCWD: t.CWD, AgentStatus: state}
	if t.Foreground != nil && t.Foreground.CWD != "" {
		p.CWD = t.Foreground.CWD
	}
	if app != "" {
		p.Agent = app
		p.AgentName = t.Name
	}
	return p
}

// CurrentPaneID implements CurrentPaneResolver from HC_TERMINAL_ID, verified
// against the live server rather than trusted as an inherited hint.
func (h *HerdrCore) CurrentPaneID(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
	address := h.getenv("HC_TERMINAL_ID")
	if address == "" {
		return "", errors.New("not inside a herdr-core terminal (HC_TERMINAL_ID is unset)")
	}
	t, err := h.terminal(ctx, address)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	return t.Address, nil
}

// AgentActivities implements AgentActivityLister. A terminal whose program hc
// recognizes as an agent occupies its foreground cwd whatever its state.
func (h *HerdrCore) AgentActivities(ctx context.Context) ([]AgentActivity, error) {
	terminals, err := h.terminals(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var out []AgentActivity
	for _, t := range terminals {
		app, state := t.status()
		if app == "" {
			continue
		}
		dirs := t.dirs()
		if len(dirs) == 0 {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("hc get %s: recognized agent has no cwd", t.Address)
		}
		out = append(out, AgentActivity{
			PaneID: t.Address, WorkspaceID: t.Labels["herdr.space"],
			Agent: app, Name: t.Name, Status: state, CWD: dirs[0],
		})
	}
	return out, nil
}

// Open implements Runtime. A space or terminal already covering dir is
// reused; otherwise Herdr Desktop gets a new unfocused space, or, without a
// window, hc gets a new detached shell terminal. Navigation calls Activate.
func (h *HerdrCore) Open(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
	existing, err := h.List(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return OpenResult{}, err
	}
	desktop := h.DesktopAvailable(ctx)
	for _, s := range existing {
		// Only a surface the person can be switched to is reusable: with a
		// window running, a bare terminal no space shows is not.
		if desktop && !isSpaceHandle(s.Handle) {
			continue
		}
		if s.Covers(dir) {
			return OpenResult{Handle: s.Handle, Surface: surfaceOf(s.Handle), Opened: true}, nil
		}
	}
	if desktop {
		return h.createSpace(ctx, dir, label)
	}
	return h.createTerminal(ctx, dir, label)
}

func (h *HerdrCore) createSpace(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
	before, err := h.spaces(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return OpenResult{}, err
	}
	known := map[string]bool{}
	for _, s := range before {
		known[s.ID] = true
	}
	args := []string{"do", "space.new", "--folder", dir, "--focus", "false"}
	if label != "" {
		args = append(args, "--name", label)
	}
	if _, err := h.app(ctx, args...); err != nil {
		return OpenResult{}, err
	}
	// The response shape of `do` is not a documented contract, so the new
	// space is identified by diffing the layout rather than by parsing it.
	after, err := h.spaces(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return OpenResult{}, err
	}
	for _, s := range after {
		if known[s.ID] {
			continue
		}
		if label != "" && s.Name != label {
			continue
		}
		res := OpenResult{Handle: s.ID, Surface: "space", Opened: true, Created: true}
		for _, address := range s.terminals() {
			if err := h.label(ctx, address, map[string]string{"owned": "1"}); err != nil {
				return res, err
			}
		}
		return res, nil
	}
	return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("herdr-app do space.new: no new space for %s appeared", dir)
}

func (h *HerdrCore) createTerminal(ctx context.Context, dir, label string) (OpenResult, error) {
	args := []string{"run", "--bg", "--json", "--no-parent", "--outlive-parent", "--cwd", dir,
		"--label", herdrCoreOwnedLabel + "=1"}
	if label != "" {
		args = append(args, "--label", herdrCoreLabelSpace+"label="+label)
	}
	raw, err := h.hc(ctx, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return OpenResult{}, err
	}
	var res struct {
		Address string `json:"address"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &res); err != nil || res.Address == "" {
		return OpenResult{}, fmt.Errorf("hc run: response has no terminal address")
	}
	return OpenResult{Handle: res.Address, Surface: "terminal", Opened: true, Created: true, RootPaneID: res.Address}, nil
}

// Activate switches Herdr Desktop to a space. A bare terminal is attached only
// from outside herdr-core: attaching inside an hc terminal would nest clients.
func (h *HerdrCore) Activate(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
	if handle == "" {
		return nil
	}
	if isSpaceHandle(handle) {
		_, err := h.app(ctx, "do", "space.select", "--id", handle)
		return err
	}
	if h.getenv("HC_TERMINAL_ID") != "" {
		return nil
	}
	return h.interactive(ctx, h.hcBin, "attach", handle)
}

// Close implements Runtime. Only surfaces dev opened are ended: every local
// terminal of a space must carry dev's ownership label, so a space a person
// added their own tabs to is refused rather than closed with their work.
func (h *HerdrCore) Close(ctx context.Context, handle string) error {
	if handle == "" {
		return nil
	}
	owned, err := h.ownedTerminals(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !isSpaceHandle(handle) {
		if !owned[handle] {
			return fmt.Errorf("herdr-core terminal %s was not opened by dev; close it yourself", handle)
		}
		_, err := h.hc(ctx, "kill", handle)
		return err
	}
	spaces, err := h.spaces(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	for _, s := range spaces {
		if s.ID != handle {
			continue
		}
		for _, address := range s.terminals() {
			if !owned[address] {
				return fmt.Errorf("herdr-core space %s holds terminal %s that dev did not open; close it yourself", handle, address)
			}
		}
		_, err := h.app(ctx, "do", "space.close", "--id", handle, "--confirmed", "true")
		return err
	}
	return nil
}

func (h *HerdrCore) ownedTerminals(ctx context.Context) (map[string]bool, error) {
	raw, err := h.hc(ctx, "ls", "--json", "--label", herdrCoreOwnedLabel+"=1")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var list hcList
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &list); err != nil || list.Terminals == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("hc ls --label: response has no terminals array")
	}
	out := map[string]bool{}
	for _, t := range *list.Terminals {
		out[t.Address] = true
	}
	return out, nil
}

// Annotate implements Runtime with dev-namespaced terminal labels on the
// session's terminals. An empty value removes the label.
func (h *HerdrCore) Annotate(ctx context.Context, handle string, kv map[string]string) error {
	if handle == "" || len(kv) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	targets := []string{handle}
	if isSpaceHandle(handle) {
		spaces, err := h.spaces(ctx)
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		targets = nil
		for _, s := range spaces {
			if s.ID == handle {
				targets = s.terminals()
			}
		}
	}
	for _, address := range targets {
		if err := h.label(ctx, address, kv); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func (h *HerdrCore) label(ctx context.Context, address string, kv map[string]string) error {
	if len(kv) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	names := make([]string, 0, len(kv))
	for k := range kv {
		names = append(names, k)
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	args := []string{"label", address}
	for _, k := range names {
		args = append(args, herdrCoreLabelSpace+k+"="+kv[k])
	}
	args = append(args, "--json")
	_, err := h.hc(ctx, args...)
	return err
}

// isSpaceHandle distinguishes Herdr Desktop space ids (`sp…`) from hc
// terminal addresses (`t7`).
func isSpaceHandle(handle string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(handle, "sp") }

func surfaceOf(handle string) string {
	if isSpaceHandle(handle) {
		return "space"
	}
	return "terminal"
}

func appendUnique(dst []string, values ...string) []string {
	for _, v := range values {
		if v == "" {
			continue
		}
		dup := false
		for _, d := range dst {
			if d == v || pathx.Same(d, v) {
				dup = true
				break
			}
		}
		if !dup {
			dst = append(dst, v)
		}
	}
	return dst
}
```

```go
package runtime

import (
	"context"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"
)

// HostKind names the terminal environment dev itself is running in. It is an
// observation of inherited caller context, independent of which runtime
// backend is configured.
type HostKind string

const (
	HostHerdr     HostKind = "herdr"
	HostHerdrCore HostKind = "herdr-core"
	HostTmux      HostKind = "tmux"
	HostZellij    HostKind = "zellij"
	HostPlain     HostKind = "plain"
)

// GUI hosts of a herdr-core terminal. Herdr Desktop and Sheprd are different
// products; GUIUnknown never becomes a guess.
const (
	GUIHerdrDesktop = "herdr-desktop"
	GUISheprd       = "sheprd"
	GUIUnknown      = "unknown"
)

// HostContext is what DetectHost observed.
type HostContext struct {
	Kind HostKind
	// GUI is set only for herdr-core: which window shows this terminal.
	GUI string
	// TerminalID is HC_TERMINAL_ID inside herdr-core.
	TerminalID string
	// Evidence lists the environment markers seen, innermost first.
	Evidence []string
}

// Describe renders the context for doctor and the dashboard.
func (c HostContext) Describe() string {
	switch c.Kind {
	case HostHerdrCore:
		gui := "GUI unknown"
		switch c.GUI {
		case GUIHerdrDesktop:
			gui = "Herdr Desktop"
		case GUISheprd:
			gui = "Sheprd"
		}
		if c.TerminalID != "" {
			return "herdr-core (" + gui + ", " + c.TerminalID + ")"
		}
		return "herdr-core (" + gui + ")"
	case "":
		return string(HostPlain)
	}
	return string(c.Kind)
}

// hostProbe carries the seams DetectHost needs.
type hostProbe struct {
	getenv func(string) string
	core   *HerdrCore
	stat   func(string) error
}

// DetectHost classifies the caller's terminal environment. Markers are read
// innermost first: a tmux started inside an hc terminal is a tmux host. The
// only process it may run is one bounded Herdr Desktop layout read to learn
// whether that window shows this terminal.
func DetectHost(ctx context.Context) HostContext {
	return detectHost(ctx, hostProbe{getenv: os.Getenv, core: NewHerdrCore(), stat: func(p string) error {
		_, err := os.Stat(p)
		return err
	}})
}

func detectHost(ctx context.Context, p hostProbe) HostContext {
	var c HostContext
	markers := []struct {
		kind HostKind
		env  string
	}{
		{HostTmux, "TMUX"}, {HostZellij, "ZELLIJ"}, {HostHerdr, "HERDR_ENV"}, {HostHerdrCore, "HC_TERMINAL_ID"},
	}
	for _, m := range markers {
		if p.getenv(m.env) == "" {
			continue
		}
		c.Evidence = append(c.Evidence, m.env)
		if c.Kind == "" {
			c.Kind = m.kind
		}
	}
	if c.Kind == "" {
		c.Kind = HostPlain
		return c
	}
	if c.Kind != HostHerdrCore {
		return c
	}
	c.TerminalID = p.getenv("HC_TERMINAL_ID")
	c.GUI = GUIUnknown
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
	defer cancel()
	if spaces, err := p.core.spaces(ctx); err == nil {
		for _, s := range spaces {
			for _, address := range s.terminals() {
				if address == c.TerminalID {
					c.GUI = GUIHerdrDesktop
					c.Evidence = append(c.Evidence, "herdr-app ls shows "+address)
					return c
				}
			}
		}
	}
	// Sheprd's control socket is only stat-ed. Its presence with this terminal
	// absent from Herdr Desktop is recorded as evidence, not a GUI claim.
	if home, err := os.UserHomeDir(); err == nil && p.stat != nil {
		if p.stat(filepath.Join(home, ".local", "state", "herdr", "gpui", "control.sock")) == nil {
			c.Evidence = append(c.Evidence, "sheprd control socket present")
		}
	}
	return c
}
```

```text
// The contract every backend must satisfy. Backends that are not installed on
// this machine are skipped rather than failed, so the suite is meaningful in
// CI (where only None exists) and locally (where herdr and tmux do).
func TestBackendContract(t *testing.T) {
	for _, rt := range runtime.All() {
		t.Run(rt.Name(), func(t *testing.T) {
			if !rt.Available() {
				t.Skipf("%s not available on this machine", rt.Name())
			}
			ctx := context.Background()
			sessions, err := rt.List(ctx)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("List on an available backend must not error: %v", err)
			}
			for _, s := range sessions {
				if s.Handle == "" {
					t.Errorf("session with empty handle: %+v", s)
				}
			}
			// Closing an unknown handle must be tolerated, not fatal: dev's
			// stored handle is advisory and often stale.
			if err := rt.Close(ctx, ""); err != nil {
				t.Errorf("Close(\"\") should be a no-op, got %v", err)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
package runtime

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// fakeHerdrCore answers hc and herdr-app calls from in-memory state and
// records every invocation.
type fakeHerdrCore struct {
	terminals map[string]string // address -> `hc get` JSON
	order     []string
	owned     []string
	spaces    string // `herdr-app ls` JSON; empty means no window
	afterNew  string // layout after space.new
	calls     []string
	env       map[string]string
	attached  []string
}

func (f *fakeHerdrCore) core() *HerdrCore {
	return &HerdrCore{
		hcBin: "herdr-core",
		runHC: func(_ context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
			f.calls = append(f.calls, "hc "+strings.Join(args, " "))
			switch {
			case len(args) >= 2 && args[0] == "server":
				return []byte(`{"version":"0.1.17"}`), nil
			case len(args) == 4 && args[0] == "ls" && args[2] == "--label":
				return []byte(listJSON(f.owned)), nil
			case args[0] == "ls":
				return []byte(listJSON(f.order)), nil
			case args[0] == "get":
				if doc, ok := f.terminals[args[1]]; ok {
					return []byte(doc), nil
				}
				return nil, errors.New("hc get: no such terminal")
			case args[0] == "run":
				return []byte(`{"address":"t9","agent":"zsh","state":"live"}`), nil
			case args[0] == "label", args[0] == "kill":
				return []byte(`{}`), nil
			}
			return nil, errors.New("unexpected hc call")
		},
		runApp: func(_ context.Context, args ...string) ([]byte, error) {
			f.calls = append(f.calls, "app "+strings.Join(args, " "))
			if f.spaces == "" {
				return nil, errors.New("herdr-app: window not running")
			}
			switch args[0] {
			case "status":
				return []byte(`{}`), nil
			case "ls":
				return []byte(f.spaces), nil
			case "do":
				if args[1] == "space.new" && f.afterNew != "" {
					f.spaces = f.afterNew
				}
				return []byte(`{}`), nil
			}
			return nil, errors.New("unexpected herdr-app call")
		},
		getenv:      func(k string) string { return f.env[k] },
		interactive: func(_ context.Context, bin string, args ...string) error { f.attached = append(f.attached, bin+" "+strings.Join(args, " ")); return nil },
	}
}

func listJSON(addresses []string) string {
	parts := make([]string, 0, len(addresses))
	for _, a := range addresses {
		parts = append(parts, `{"address":"`+a+`","state":"live"}`)
	}
	return `{"terminals":[` + strings.Join(parts, ",") + `]}`
}

func (f *fakeHerdrCore) called(prefix string) bool {
	for _, c := range f.calls {
		if strings.HasPrefix(c, prefix) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

		spaces: twoSpaces,
		env:    map[string]string{},
	}
}

func TestHerdrCoreListGroupsSpacesAndSkipsRemoteTerminals(t *testing.T) {
	f := standardTerminals()
	sessions, err := f.core().List(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(sessions) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("sessions = %+v, want the local space and the loose terminal", sessions)
	}
	space := sessions[0]
	if space.Handle != "sp1" || !space.Focused || len(space.Panes) != 2 || space.AgentStatus != "working" {
		t.Fatalf("space session = %+v", space)
	}
	if !space.Covers("/code/dev-cli") || space.Covers("/code/other") {
		t.Fatalf("space dirs = %v: must cover the agent's foreground cwd, not siblings", space.Dirs)
	}
	if space.Panes[0].Agent != "claude-code" || space.Panes[0].CWD != "/code/dev-cli" || space.Panes[1].Agent != "" {
		t.Fatalf("panes = %+v", space.Panes)
	}
	if loose := sessions[1]; loose.Handle != "t4" || loose.Label != "loose" || !loose.Covers("/code/other") {
		t.Fatalf("loose session = %+v", loose)
	}
	if f.called("hc get box/t1") {
		t.Fatal("remote machine terminals must not be observed as local")
	}
}

func TestHerdrCoreAgentActivitiesReportEveryRecognizedAgent(t *testing.T) {
	f := standardTerminals()
	activities, err := f.core().AgentActivities(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(activities) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("activities = %+v, want only the recognized agent", activities)
	}
	a := activities[0]
	if a.PaneID != "t2" || a.Agent != "claude-code" || a.CWD != "/code/dev-cli" || a.WorkspaceID != "sp1" || a.Status != "working" {
		t.Fatalf("activity = %+v", a)
	}
}

func TestHerdrCoreObservationFailsClosedWhenATerminalCannotBeRead(t *testing.T) {
	f := standardTerminals()
	delete(f.terminals, "t3")
	if _, err := f.core().AgentActivities(context.Background()); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("an unreadable terminal must fail agent observation rather than look unoccupied")
	}
}

func TestHerdrCoreOpenReusesCoveringSpace(t *testing.T) {
	f := standardTerminals()
	res, err := f.core().Open(context.Background(), "/code/dev-cli", "dev-cli")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res.Handle != "sp1" || res.Created || res.Surface != "space" {
		t.Fatalf("open = %+v", res)
	}
	if f.called("app do space.new") {
		t.Fatal("a covering space must be reused")
	}
}

func TestHerdrCoreOpenCreatesUnfocusedSpaceAndLabelsIt(t *testing.T) {
	f := standardTerminals()
	f.afterNew = strings.Replace(twoSpaces, `{"spaces":[`, `{"spaces":[
 {"id":"sp7","name":"fresh","folder":"/code/fresh","machine":null,"active":false,"tabs":[
  {"id":"tb7","name":"1","active":true,"terminals":[{"terminal":"t8","pane":"p8"}]}]},`, 1)
	res, err := f.core().Open(context.Background(), "/code/fresh", "fresh")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res.Handle != "sp7" || !res.Created {
		t.Fatalf("open = %+v", res)
	}
	if !f.called("app do space.new --folder /code/fresh --focus false --name fresh") {
		t.Fatalf("calls = %v", f.calls)
	}
	if !f.called("hc label t8 dev.owned=1") {

func TestHerdrCoreOpenWithoutWindowStartsDetachedTerminal(t *testing.T) {

func TestHerdrCoreActivateNeverNestsInsideAnHCTerminal(t *testing.T) {
	f := standardTerminals()
	f.env["HC_TERMINAL_ID"] = "t2"
	core := f.core()
	if err := core.Activate(context.Background(), "sp1"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !f.called("app do space.select --id sp1") {
		t.Fatalf("space activation must select it in Herdr Desktop; calls = %v", f.calls)
	}
	if err := core.Activate(context.Background(), "t4"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(f.attached) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("attached %v inside an hc terminal", f.attached)
	}
	delete(f.env, "HC_TERMINAL_ID")
	if err := core.Activate(context.Background(), "t4"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(f.attached) != 1 || f.attached[0] != "herdr-core attach t4" {
		t.Fatalf("attached = %v", f.attached)
	}
}

func TestHerdrCoreCloseRequiresDevOwnership(t *testing.T) {
	f := standardTerminals()
	f.owned = []string{"t2"}
	if err := f.core().Close(context.Background(), "sp1"); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "t3") {
		t.Fatalf("Close of a space with a foreign terminal = %v, want refusal naming it", err)
	}
	if f.called("app do space.close") {
		t.Fatal("a space with a foreign terminal must not be closed")
	}
	if err := f.core().Close(context.Background(), "t4"); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("a terminal dev did not open must not be killed")
	}
	f.owned = []string{"t2", "t3", "t4"}
	if err := f.core().Close(context.Background(), "sp1"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !f.called("app do space.close --id sp1 --confirmed true") {
		t.Fatalf("calls = %v", f.calls)
	}
	if err := f.core().Close(context.Background(), "t4"); err != nil || !f.called("hc kill t4") {
		t.Fatalf("Close(t4) = %v; calls = %v", err, f.calls)
	}
}

	f := standardTerminals()

func TestDetectHost(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name   string
		env    map[string]string
		spaces string
		kind   HostKind
		gui    string
	}{
		{name: "plain", env: map[string]string{}, kind: HostPlain},
		{name: "classic herdr", env: map[string]string{"HERDR_ENV": "1"}, kind: HostHerdr},
		{name: "herdr desktop", env: map[string]string{"HC_TERMINAL_ID": "t2"}, spaces: twoSpaces, kind: HostHerdrCore, gui: GUIHerdrDesktop},
		{name: "hc without window", env: map[string]string{"HC_TERMINAL_ID": "t2"}, kind: HostHerdrCore, gui: GUIUnknown},
		{name: "terminal not shown", env: map[string]string{"HC_TERMINAL_ID": "t77"}, spaces: twoSpaces, kind: HostHerdrCore, gui: GUIUnknown},
		{name: "tmux inside hc", env: map[string]string{"HC_TERMINAL_ID": "t2", "TMUX": "/tmp/tmux"}, spaces: twoSpaces, kind: HostTmux},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := standardTerminals()
			f.spaces, f.env = tc.spaces, tc.env
			got := detectHost(context.Background(), hostProbe{getenv: f.core().getenv, core: f.core(), stat: func(string) error { return errors.New("absent") }})
			if got.Kind != tc.kind || got.GUI != tc.gui {
				t.Fatalf("detectHost = %+v, want kind %s gui %q", got, tc.kind, tc.gui)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestInsideHerdrCoreOnly(t *testing.T) {
	env := func(m map[string]string) func(string) string { return func(k string) string { return m[k] } }
	if !insideHerdrCoreOnly(env(map[string]string{"HC_TERMINAL_ID": "t1"})) {
		t.Fatal("hc terminal must prefer herdr-core")
	}
	for _, inner := range []string{"HERDR_ENV", "TMUX", "ZELLIJ"} {
		if insideHerdrCoreOnly(env(map[string]string{"HC_TERMINAL_ID": "t1", inner: "1"})) {
			t.Fatalf("an inner %s must keep its own backend", inner)
		}
	}
}
```

```text
func applyTryAction(ctx context.Context, app *App, rt runtime.Runtime, request tui.TryRequest) (tui.TryActionResult, error) {
	service, err := newExperimentService(app)
	if err != nil {
		return tui.TryActionResult{}, err
	}
	resolve := func() (experiment.Item, error) {
		item, diagnostics, resolveErr := service.ResolveWithOptions(ctx, request.ID, experiment.ResolveOptions{
			IncludeDeprecated: true, IncludeArchived: true,
			IncludeEvicted: true, IncludeGraduated: true,
		})
		warnExperimentDiagnostics(app, diagnostics)
		return item, resolveErr
	}
	open := func(item experiment.Item, status string) (tui.TryActionResult, error) {
		if item.Entry == nil {
			return tui.TryActionResult{}, errors.New("Try catalog identity is unavailable")
		}
		location, located := item.Entry.LocationFor(config.Hostname())
		if !located || location.State != catalog.LocationPresent || item.Entry.MoveIntent != nil {
			return tui.TryActionResult{}, errors.New("restore or reconcile this Try before opening it")
		}

		if !item.Live.Present || item.Live.CurrentPath == "" {
			return tui.TryActionResult{}, fmt.Errorf("Try %s is not present on this host", item.DisplayName())
		}
		handle, openErr := openCheckout(ctx, rt, item.Live.CurrentPath, item.DisplayName())
		if openErr != nil {
			return tui.TryActionResult{}, openErr
		}
		result := tui.TryActionResult{Status: status, RefreshRepos: true}
```

```text
func (m *Model) finishRemoteCloneState() tea.Cmd {
	deferred := m.remoteClone.deferredOpen
	m.remoteClone = remoteCloneState{}
	if deferred.Directory != "" {
		m.chosen, m.quitting = deferred.Directory, true
		return tea.Quit
	}
	if deferred.RuntimeHandle != "" {
		m.activate, m.quitting = deferred.RuntimeHandle, true
		return tea.Quit
	}
	return nil
}
```

```text
func (m Model) openSelectedIn(target string) tea.Cmd {
	ctx := WithOpenTarget(context.Background(), target)
	if row, ok := m.currentTask(); ok {
		if err := taskOpenBlocker(row); err != nil {
			return func() tea.Msg { return actionMsg{err: err} }

		}

			return openedMsg(opened, err)
		}
	}
	if item, ok := m.currentRepoItem(); ok && item.child() {
		checkout, _ := item.checkout()
		dir := checkout.Worktree.Path
		return func() tea.Msg {
			if !checkout.Exists || checkout.Worktree.Prunable {
				return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("worktree checkout is missing or prunable: %s", dir)}
			}
			if m.actions.OpenCheckout == nil {
				return actionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("opening linked worktrees is unavailable")}
			}
			opened, err := m.actions.OpenCheckout(ctx, item.Repo, checkout)
			return openedMsg(opened, err)
		}
	}
	if r, ok := m.currentTry(); ok {
		if !r.Present() {
			return func() tea.Msg {
				return tryActionMsg{err: fmt.Errorf("Try %s is %s on this host", r.Item.DisplayName(), r.Where())}
			}
		}
		return m.applyTryIn(ctx, TryRequest{Action: TryOpen, ID: r.reference()})
	}
	if r, ok := m.currentRemote(); ok {
		if !r.Cloned() {
			return nil // c is the explicit clone action
```
